title: Mosaiko — Chocolate Biscuit Salami
style: No-bake Greek chocolate biscuit salami (mosaiko / kormos / doukissa) with fruit preserves, rolled into logs and coated in ganache.
description: A no-bake Greek chocolate biscuit salami — a rich cocoa buttercream folded through milk-soaked biscuits, rolled into two logs around cherry and fig preserves, then coated in white and raspberry-chocolate ganache. Makes two logs.

items.note: such as Marie, morning coffee, or petit beurre

items.item: fig preserves with roasted nut filling

items.note: or 100 ml milk plus 1 tbsp butter

steps: Leave the butter out of the fridge for 2 hours to soften.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa powder together.
Melt the dark chocolate over a double boiler (bain-marie) and set aside to cool.

Beat the butter, cocoa powder, and icing sugar with a hand mixer on low speed until fluffy. Add the melted chocolate, coarse sea salt, and raspberry essence, then mix to combine, increasing the speed.
In a separate bowl, break the biscuits into smaller pieces and pour over the milk. Mix quickly so they are evenly wet.
Add the biscuits to the buttercream gradually, folding with a spatula until all are incorporated.
Cut two big pieces of parchment paper and lay a piece of cling film on top of each.
Divide the mixture along the centre of both cling films, flattening it out.
Spoon the cherry preserve along the centre of one; on the other, place the halved fig preserves cut-side up along the centre.
Using the cling film to help, fold each into a salami shape and roll until round, then wrap in the cling film.
Wrap again with the parchment paper and refrigerate for a couple of hours before coating.

White chocolate coating: Put the 40 ml cream in a microwave-safe bowl, break in the white chocolate, and heat on medium for 1 minute. Stir until melted, repeating for 30 seconds if needed. Let it cool slightly, then coat the cherry log.
Chocolate ganache: Make a ganache with the raspberry chocolate and 100 ml cream using the double-boiler method, then coat the fig log.
Store in the fridge until the chocolate sets. You can also freeze once set — wrap again in cling film. If frozen, let it sit at room temperature for a few minutes before cutting or serving.
tips: The logs can stay in the freezer for a long time before coating. If already coated, freeze them first and then wrap in cling film.
The first time you freeze them, place them on a flat surface such as a tray so they don't break.
Draining the cherry preserve well keeps the filling from making the log soggy.
Chill the logs thoroughly before coating so the warm ganache sets quickly and evenly.
